beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI cold open. Ask lands answered; narration introduces Liam in for Bear.
beats.narration_text: Sawubona, this is Liam, in for Bear. There are over seven thousand icons in Brutalist. Nobody remembers them. So when you need a mark for a beat, the first move is not to draw. It is to search. Art icons is the library-first check that stops one-off scribbles from piling up in svg.

props.command: Before drawing a mark for a beat, ask the library: is there already an icon for this?
output: ranked: exact name > every word > prefix > token hit (IDF)
aliases: icons, icon, icon-search — same case branch, same output

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — Beat 2 BLUF, written by the hesitant writer. Corrects the reel's actual misconception.
beats.narration_text: Watch the writer walk this back. Art icons does not draw a new icon for you. It finds an existing one, from the seven-thousand icon set. Same command, different job — and it is the difference this whole reel turns on.

show.event: three lines type down the frame: 'art icons / draws / new icons.'
the word 'draws' turns terracotta, hesitates, backspaces, types 'finds'
the word 'new' turns terracotta, hesitates, backspaces, types 'existing'
final corrected stack settles: 'art icons / finds / existing icons.'

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the shape of the dispatcher. One case branch, three aliases, one exec.
beats.narration_text: The dispatcher is a single case statement in the art file. One branch matches three aliases: the word icons, the singular icon, and the long form icon-search. All three exec the same python script. Different words on your terminal, one code path underneath.

show.event: code card fades in with 'art' in the title bar
three alias patterns type on the same line
spark line settles under the card

props.title: art:60-63 — one branch, three aliases
props.code:
# From the top-level art dispatcher:
case "$cmd" in
  # …
  icons|icon|icon-search)
    # LIBRARY-FIRST, one level down from scenes:
    # find the mark before drawing one.
    exec python3 "$ART_HOME/runtime/scripts/icon_search.py" "$@"
    ;;
  # …
esac
props.sparkLine: Three words. One script. One index.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — the canonical set. Numbers, geometry, stroke, invariants.
beats.narration_text: The library the script searches is a single JSON file at icons dot json. Seven thousand three hundred and thirty icons. Three hundred and seventy-six of them are brand or logo marks. Every icon is a twenty-four unit viewBox, stroke width two, currentColor. That means one component style, one accent hook. They compose.

show.event: card in; title reads 'icons/icons.json — the canonical set'
sample icon record types under it

props.sparkLine: One viewBox. One stroke. One color hook.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — the ranking. Four moves, then IDF re-weighting so rare words win.
beats.narration_text: The ranker has one job: put the right hit at the top. Four rules, in order of trust. Exact name beats every-word-present, beats name-prefix, beats token-hit. Then it re-weights by inverse document frequency. That means a rare word like sankey outranks a common word like flow, so 'sankey flow' finds chart-sankey and not every flower in the set.

show.event: four ranking rules type as a bulleted block

props.title: icon_search.py — rank()  (art icons ranking)
props.code:
# Most trusted first — the four moves:
#
#     exact name  >  every query word present
#                  >  name prefix
#                  >  token hit
#
# Then RE-WEIGHT by inverse document frequency (IDF):
idf = { w: math.log((n + 1) / (df.get(w, 0) + 1)) + 1
        for w in words }

# Effect: a rare word beats a common one.
#   'sankey flow'  ->  chart-sankey  (not every 'flower' in the set)
#   'data database' -> database      ('database' is rarer than 'data')
props.sparkLine: Exact > all-words > prefix > token. Rare wins.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — verbatim output of ./art icons "money" from this workspace.
beats.narration_text: Here is the shape on a real query. Dot slash art icons quote money quote. Thirty-one hits. Top ten shown. First hit is money-square from Iconoir. Then banknote, coins, wallet from Lucide. Each line shows the name, the source pack, and the svg path. The tokens underneath tell you which words the ranker matched.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — --check and --show. The anti-redraw test and the raw SVG.
beats.narration_text: Two more moves. Dash dash check is the anti-redraw question — is this name in the set. It answers three things per name: in set, concept or brand, and the file path. If you missed, it shows you the nearest neighbors. Dash dash show prints the raw SVG, so you can paste it into a component or a mood board without opening the file.

show.event: --show SVG one-liner types under a divider

props.title: --check (anti-redraw)  and  --show (raw SVG)
props.code:
$ ./art icons --check brain-circuit database bogus-icon-name
  brain-circuit       IN SET   concept    svg/brain-circuit.svg
  database            IN SET   concept    svg/database.svg
  bogus-icon-name     not in the set.

# ------------------------------------------------------------

$ ./art icons --show database
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24"
     viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
     stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">
  <ellipse cx="12" cy="5" rx="9" ry="3" />
  <path d="M3 5V19A9 3 0 0 0 21 19V5" />
  <path d="M3 12A9 3 0 0 0 21 12" />
</svg>

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — --brands filter. Two logos for 'github' in the whole set.
beats.narration_text: One filter changes the whole answer. Dash dash brands narrows the search to the three hundred and seventy-six brand and logo icons only. Search github with the filter and you get two hits, both logos. Drop the filter and the ranker starts pulling in concept icons that happen to share tokens. The filter is a scope switch, not a preference.

show.event: card in; title reads '--brands  (scope switch, not preference)'
filtered run types in and returns two hits

props.title: $ ./art icons "github" --brands   (filter to brand/logo)
props.code:
$ ./art icons "github" --brands
2 match "github" - top 2:

  brand-github            brand   svg/brand-github.svg
     brand github
  brand-github-copilot    brand   svg/brand-github-copilot.svg
     brand copilot github

# The mirror flag:
$ ./art icons "github" --no-brands       # exclude every logo

# --brands narrows the corpus to 376 brand/logo icons.
# --no-brands narrows it to the 6,954 concept icons.
# Neither reranks — they just decide which shelf to search.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — the miss. The tool prints an explicit anti-redraw instruction; exit 0.
beats.narration_text: And here is what a miss looks like. Quantum entanglement. No match. The tool does not silently return empty. It prints an instruction: a miss is not a licence to draw. Try a nearby concept. Compose two icons. Or accept that the idea is not iconographic. Exit code zero, because the answer 'nothing fits' is the real answer.

show.event: card in; title reads '$ ./art icons "quantum entanglement"'
'no icon matches …' line appears in terracotta

props.title: $ ./art icons "quantum entanglement"   (the miss)
props.code:
$ ./art icons "quantum entanglement"
no icon matches "quantum entanglement".
  A miss is NOT a licence to draw a one-off. Try a nearby concept,
  compose two icons, or accept the idea is not iconographic.

$ echo $?
0

# The doctrine, spelled out. From icon_search.py:
#
#   'if nothing fits, the honest answers are
#    (a) a nearby concept, (b) compose two icons, or
#    (c) the concept genuinely is not iconographic.'
props.sparkLine: A miss is the answer. Not a licence to draw.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the four moves. One line each, in the order you actually use them.
beats.narration_text: So the surface. Bare art icons prints the info banner and exits. A query searches the whole set with IDF ranking. Dash dash check answers is-it-in-the-set. Dash dash show hands you the raw SVG. Dash dash brands narrows the corpus to the three hundred and seventy-six logos. Three aliases all point at the same script. And a miss is a real answer, not a licence to draw.

props.artifactHeading: art icons — the whole surface, in the order you actually use it
artifactLines: bare invocation — prints the info banner (7,330 count, viewBox, examples) and exits 0.
"query" — searches all 7,330 icons; exact name > all-words present > prefix > token hit, IDF re-weighted.
--check <name...> — asks 'is this name in the set?' — the anti-redraw test that stops one-off scribbles.
--show <name> — prints the raw SVG straight to stdout for pasting into a component or mood board.
--brands / --no-brands — scope switch: search only 376 logos, or only the 6,954 concept icons.
aliases icons / icon / icon-search — same case branch, identical output; one dispatcher, one code path.
a miss — no match found; 'not a licence to draw' — try a nearby concept or compose two icons.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code from the brutalist toolkit root. It walks the whole surface: banner, three search runs of different rarity, a check pair, a show, a brands filter, and one deliberate miss. What you want to see is fair ranking on common words, the rare word winning where it should, three passing checks, one honest miss, and identical output across the three aliases. If any run surprises you, that is a lead — file it against icon_search.py rank.
